findings.evidence_span: joint decoding recovered 99.5\% of
findings.rationale: class 1 (Abstract, main.tex:L30): "joint decoding" is the paper's central coined term but is never defined; the abstract uses it cold, and the body never says it is the same thing as the "Grid" method or "the grid decoder".
findings.suggested_fix: Define it once at first use ("decoding all cards together, which we call joint decoding") and state at line 392 that the Grid method is joint decoding.

findings.evidence_span: $t$ of $n$ cards recover the secret, fewer reveal nothing, every card repairs
findings.rationale: class 1 (Abstract, main.tex:L28): "card" appears with no statement that a card is one share written as a phrase; the body (lines 204-207) also uses it without ever saying so.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "each share is a phrase written on one card" at first use, and repeat the definition at line 204.

findings.evidence_span: itself, and spare cards repair each other. In fault injection
findings.rationale: class 1 (Abstract, main.tex:L29): "spare cards" is used here and in the Introduction (line 76) but only becomes inferable at line 496 ("the single spare card of a 2-of-3 set"); it is never defined as cards beyond the threshold t.
findings.suggested_fix: Define it at first use: "spare cards (those beyond the t needed)".

findings.evidence_span: In 31{,}600 trials the decoder returned no wrong secret.
findings.rationale: class 1 (Abstract, main.tex:L34): The count has no referent: the body (line 531) restricts it to grid trials and to the two methods with a digest, while single-phrase trials and digest-free methods did return wrong answers.
findings.suggested_fix: Write "In 31,600 grid trials the decoders that check the digest returned no wrong secret".

findings.evidence_span: they compose into a product
findings.rationale: class 1 (1 Introduction, main.tex:L47): "product code" is used as the key structural idea but never defined; the stated audience is assumed to know Reed-Solomon basics, not product codes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one clause: "a product code, i.e. an array whose every row is a codeword of one code and every column a codeword of another".

findings.evidence_span: happens to be the locator of one of the $L$
findings.rationale: class 1 (3.2 Repair beyond substitutions, main.tex:L190): "locator" is never defined; the reader must infer that it means alpha^p for a position p.
findings.suggested_fix: Write "equals $\alpha^{p}$ for one of the $L$ positions $p$".

findings.evidence_span: A 24+2 phrase has 325 possible
findings.rationale: class 1 (3.2 Repair beyond substitutions, main.tex:L191): The "N+k" shorthand (24+2, 12+2, and so on) is used here and as the Table 1 column heads without ever being introduced.
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce it in Section 3.1: "we write N+k for a phrase of N data words and k parity words".

findings.evidence_span: the row decoder as a known symbol
findings.rationale: class 1 (4.2 Reading the header, main.tex:L282): "the row decoder" is used before the Rows step of Section 4.4 and is never defined as the single-phrase repair of Section 3.
findings.suggested_fix: Write "the single-card repair of Section 3 (the row decoder)" at first use.

findings.evidence_span: Everything inside the capacity~\eqref{eq:cap} is repaired, as it must be.
findings.rationale: class 1 (5.2 Single phrases, main.tex:L404): "capacity" is coined here for the condition 2e+s<=k, which Section 3.1 called "the standard guarantee"; "beyond the capacity of $k=2$" then follows without a definition.
findings.suggested_fix: Name inequality (2) "the capacity" where it is stated (line 147) and use that name throughout.

findings.evidence_span: numbers illegible, 3\% wrong
findings.rationale: class 1 (5.3 Grids (Table 2), main.tex:L468): This fault row, discussed at line 523, is missing from the fault list in Setup (lines 371-380), so the reader does not know what was done to the cards.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an "illegible number" item to the fault list saying the card number is withheld from the decoder.

findings.evidence_span: \emph{Grid}: the decoder of Section~\ref{sec:decoder}, with the digest.
findings.rationale: class 2 (5.1 Setup, main.tex:L392): One method goes by "joint decoding", "Grid", "the grid decoder", "decoded together", "decoded as one object" and "decoding across cards/shares"; "grid" is also the name of the share format and of a dealt set.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one name for the method and use it in the abstract, method list, table head, figure legend and prose.

findings.evidence_span: repairing cards one at a time recovers 31\%, because three of the five cards
findings.rationale: class 2 (5.3 Grids, main.tex:L495): The baseline is variously "repairing cards separately", "repairing cards one at a time", "per-card repair", "Card parity", "per-share correction" and "repair card by card", and the prose does not say whether it means the Card parity or the Card parity + digest column.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the table's column label in the prose, or define "per-card repair" as that column once.

findings.evidence_span: \emph{Checksum only}: a card counts only if it is exactly valid as
findings.rationale: class 2 (5.1 Setup, main.tex:L383): "Checksum" elsewhere means the BIP39 SHA-256 checksum (also called "the BIP39 filter" and "the filter"), but here it means the Reed-Solomon validity check used for detection only.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the baseline (for example "Detect only") or state that the checksum here is the card's own parity.

findings.evidence_span: by word to parity phrases
findings.rationale: class 2 (1 Introduction, main.tex:L71): The single-phrase object is called "parity phrases" here, "protected phrase" at line 137, "single phrases" in Section 5 and "unshared 24-word phrase" at line 657.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one term (for example "protected phrase") and use it everywhere.

findings.evidence_span: sense of~\eqref{eq:syn} with length $L=W+1$.
findings.rationale: class 2 (4.1 Construction, main.tex:L210): $L$ is rebound from $N+k$ (Section 3) to $W+1$, and the data-word count changes from $N$ to $D$, so equation (1) must be re-read with new meanings.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one symbol set, or flag the change: "in this section the row length is $W+1$, with $D$ playing the role of $N$".

findings.evidence_span: (d) The stripped cards of any $m\ge t$ holders, read as an $m\times W$ array,
findings.rationale: class 2 (4.1 Construction, main.tex:L251): The people who hold cards are "holders", "parties", "participants", "people" and "backup holders", and here $m$ counts holders although it means cards (a holder may have several, as in Section 6).
findings.suggested_fix: Write "any $m\ge t$ cards" and use "holder" consistently for the person.

findings.evidence_span: Scheme & Cards & 1\% & 3\% & 5\% & Garbage & Foreign & Burnt \\
findings.rationale: class 2 (6 Custody Arrangements (Table 4), main.tex:L581): A t-of-n instance is a "set" (abstract), a "dealing" (line 204), a "sharing" (line 60), a "Scheme" (this table) and an "arrangement" (Section 6), while "scheme" also means Shamir's scheme and the paper's whole design (line 539).
findings.suggested_fix: Reserve "dealing" for one dealt set, "t-of-n set" for the parameters, and "scheme" for the design.

findings.rationale: class 2 (6 Custody Arrangements, main.tex:L607): "burnt" here reads as a destroyed card, but "burn" is defined at line 374 as a run of unreadable words and "Burnt" is a Table 4 column with that meaning.
findings.suggested_fix: Write "lost or destroyed", or say explicitly that this refers to the Burnt column.

findings.suggested_fix: Use "foreign card" (and "garbage card") consistently and keep "wrong" for words and outcomes.
